title: Reported artifact output is not equivalent to repository-observed presence

observed: The canonical ACTIVE_QUEUE contains no item owned by continuity_mining.
A prior team output named operations/continuity/claims/CM-0010-peer-trigger-evidence-boundary.json and operations/queue-updates/CM-009-2026-07-12T0504-0400.json as committed artifacts.
Direct repository fetches for both named paths returned 404 Not Found during this run.
CURRENT_STATE requires that deployment or peer execution not be claimed without evidence.
inferred: A user-facing report of a file or commit is not sufficient evidence that the artifact exists in the repository.
Continuity records should distinguish reported output from repository-observed output.
proposed: Every future team completion record should include an independently refetched repository path and blob SHA before describing a file as committed.
When a reported path cannot be refetched, record the state as unresolved_repository_presence rather than committed.
superseded: Treating a prior assistant completion statement alone as proof that a repository artifact exists.
unresolved: Whether the previously reported artifacts were committed under different paths, on a non-default branch, later removed, or never created cannot be determined from the available repository file interface in this run.

falsification_route: Refetch either previously reported artifact from the repository default branch or locate it on another branch with a valid immutable blob SHA. If found, update this claim with the observed path, ref, and SHA rather than deleting this history.
